title: Each list item under a "For the owner:" heading reaches Home as a line for the owner, with its tasks and whether it is settled
prompt:
Read crates/spawn-cli/src/serve/attention.rs (`said`, `for_owner`: how /api/attention takes the supervisor's lines for the owner from its transcript) and web/src/home.ts (`latestNotes`, Home's "From the supervisor" card). This objective comes after 064, whose `tasks` and `settled` it relies on.

The problem. On 2026-11-12 at 00:52 the supervisor wrote its asks to the owner as a heading over a list: "For the owner:", then "- If the RSI resident stays idle on task 271, restart it or reassign the task", a request to set SPAWN_WORKSPACE, and "- Reports 198, 204, 208 and 211 (missions 7/8) are still waiting for your ccd review". At 01:05 the live `/api/attention` (read-only) had `supervisor.for_owner` [], and Home showed none of them (rev-g, sync/incident-2026-11-12-claude-projects/message-not-taken.md addendum; sync/backlog.md S18). `for_owner` takes only a line that itself starts with "For the owner:". A heading's empty words are dropped, and the items under it start with "- ", so they don't match. In the supervisor's history, 19 of its 217 owner blocks are headings over lists: about 9% of what it writes for the owner never reaches Home, real asks among them.

Required behaviour.
(a) A "For the owner:" line with no words after it is a heading. That holds after any list marker, quote or emphasis, as today, so "**For the owner:**" is one.
- Each list item right after a heading ("- ", "* " or "<n>. ", after any indent), up to a blank line or a line that is no item, is a `supervisor.for_owner` item. Its text is the item's words without the marker, and its time is the turn's.
- The heading itself is no item.
- An inline "For the owner: ..." line is as today, and a list under any other heading is not the owner's.
(b) Each such item carries `tasks` and `settled` as an inline line does (objective 064). It counts toward the shown limit like any other line.
(c) Home's card shows and counts the items like any other line, and leaves a settled one out.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/070.sh.
- Setup: a real `spawn loop` runs with the supervisor on, a fake engine writes each turn to its transcript as Claude Code does, and `spawn serve` answers. One review mission's tasks 2 to 5 are set up: 2 and 3 accepted and 4 cancelled by the owner, 5 reported.
- The supervisor then writes three turns:
  - a heading over a dash list of three items ("Reports 2, 3 and 4 are still waiting for your review.", "If task 5 stays idle, restart it or reassign it.", "Set SPAWN_WORKSPACE on the host."), then a blank line, then "Next:" over a list of its own;
  - "**For the owner:**" over a numbered list of two ("Deploy main to pick up the cost page.", "Mission #3 has no backlog yet."), then a line that is no item;
  - "For the owner: task #5 waits for your review." inline.
- (1) The `for_owner` texts are exactly those six. There is no item for the heading, the "Next:" list or the line after the numbered list.
- (2) The reports item has tasks 2, 3 and 4 (accepted, accepted, cancelled) and is settled. The task 5 item has task 5 (reported) and is not settled. The SPAWN_WORKSPACE and mission #3 items name no task. Every list item carries the turn's time.
- (3) Under node, latestNotes shows the inline line first, and shown plus more is 5: the settled item is left out.
It fails with 1 on ecb177ab: only the inline line is an item. A solver must keep 064's checks green as well.

The product reason. What the supervisor writes for the owner is how the fleet asks for decisions it cannot make itself. A tenth of those asks silently never reached the page, including a stalled task's restart that night. With every item under the heading on Home, an ask is seen however the supervisor formats it, and 064's settled rule keeps finished business off the card.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/, web/test/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base, any lint relaxation and any build-time code. The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host. Keep every existing check green and add tests of your own for the new behaviour: attention.rs tests for (a) and (b) (dash, star and numbered items; the list ended by a blank line and by a non-item line; another heading's list ignored; an inline line unchanged; an item's tasks and settled), and a web/test test for (c) if home.ts changes.
